item.title: Lilly Retatrutide Triple G Obesity
item.description:
• Summary: Multiple outlets report Phase 3 obesity trial results for Eli Lilly's triple‑agonist retatrutide, which targets GLP‑1, GIP, and glucagon receptors. The drug achieved weight loss comparable to bariatric surgery, with deep reductions in body weight. Data also suggest high discontinuation rates, possibly due to gastrointestinal side effects. Despite this, retatrutide is positioned as a leading late‑stage obesity asset, potentially surpassing existing incretin therapies.
  • MoAs: Retatrutide is a triple hormone receptor agonist: GLP‑1 receptor agonist (promotes insulin secretion, delays gastric emptying, increases satiety), GIP receptor agonist (enhances insulin secretion and may improve energy expenditure), and glucagon receptor agonist (increases energy expenditure and lipolysis). The combination produces additive weight loss.
  • Sources: BioPharma Dive, Fierce Biotech, BioSpace, Endpoints News, STAT News
